source.quote: NuPrime's own page for the Hi-mDAC, read 2026-11-25 in full: « Input: 1 X USB (32-bit/384kHz & DSD256 decoding) »; « Output: 3.5mm analog or 3.5mm optical (PCM 192kHz, DoP64) »; « 32-bit/384kHz PCM and native DSD 256 decoding ». Converter: « Hi-mDAC utilizes a new chip CS43131 from Cirrus Logic. » Filters: « the CS43131 is designed with proprietary digital-interpolation filters that support five selectable digital filter responses. Filtering options include low group delay with pseudo-linear phase and a fast or slow roll-off. » Also « Asynchronous transfer mode for doubled jitter-reduction at data input and over-sampling filter stages ». The word NOS does not appear.

facts.chip: « a new chip CS43131 from Cirrus Logic ».

device_settings.why: « five selectable digital filter responses. Filtering options include low group delay with pseudo-linear phase and a fast or slow roll-off. » FIVE filters, and the maker describes three characteristics rather than naming five options - so the list cannot be reconstructed. No value is recorded. It is the eighth maker in three days to state a filter COUNT and withhold the names, and the first to describe some of them without naming any.

_verification_des_conditions_faite: nuprimeaudio.com has no terms-of-use page: the footer offers Contact & Support, a Privacy Policy, Facebook and an email address. The privacy policy WAS READ and carries no clause on copying, reproducing or extracting site content. The footer reads « Copyright 2026 (c) Nuprime Audio, Inc. --- brand managed by Nuoem Pte. Ltd. », the ordinary notice.
_un_dongle_avec_une_seule_entree_et_une_: « Input: 1 X USB » and « Output: 3.5mm analog or 3.5mm optical (PCM 192kHz, DoP64) ». One input, so the device figure IS the input figure. The 192 kHz and DoP64 belong to the OUTPUT and are not written - the same output-row trap as FiiO's and Aurender's pages, in the smallest product the catalogue holds.
